thread:
maya: ALB target group started deregistering ~20 pods in us-west-2 gpu-edge pool during a scheduled GPU scale-up. ALB health checks were returning 503s. Anyone see egress/NAT port pressure around that time?

leo: seeing it too. CloudWatch target health shows repeated 503s and connection resets. This coincided with a large model rollout where nodes pulled model blobs from S3 concurrently.

julia: can you paste the ALB event? 503 could be app-level or TCP-level misproxy.

maya: paste from the ALB events and kubectl output:
```text
[ALB] Target deregistered: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:...:targetgroup/tg-edge/abc123 reason=Unhealthy,http_code=503
kubectl get pods -n gpu-edge | grep Running | wc -l -> 42 before, 22 after deregister
```

ops-jen: classic symptom of SNAT/ephemeral port pressure — lots of outbound TLS connections to S3 from many pods will exhaust NAT ports and cause new connections (like healthchecks) to fail or be reset. Check conntrack and ephemeral port usage on worker nodes.

leo: ran quick checks on gpu-edge-12 (one of the affected nodes):
```bash
sudo conntrack -S | grep entries
conntrack entries: 198000
ss -tn state established | wc -l -> 980
cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range -> 32768 60999
```
We also saw hundreds of short-lived outbound sockets during model pulls.

julia: that port range gives ~28k ephemeral ports per node. If each pod opens many concurrent TLS streams (downloads, telemetry), it's easy to spike. ALB healthchecks often reuse source ports and can get RST if SNAT mapping gets reused/recycled. That can show up as 503 at ALB level.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-274 (priority P2) — ALB healthcheck 503 spike causing target deregistration in us-west-2 gpu-edge pool.

ezra: quick mitigation options: 1) throttle concurrent model pulls with initContainer backoff or a shared prefetch DaemonSet; 2) increase node egress capacity by adding NAT IPs / additional NAT gateways; 3) pre-warm models on nodes (image+model prefetch) to avoid many simultaneous outbound connections at scale-up; 4) tune readinessProbe to avoid marking pod NotReady while model download is ongoing.

ops-jen: also check kube-proxy/ipvs conntrack settings and ip-masq-agent — we should avoid unnecessary SNAT for intra-cluster traffic and only SNAT to NAT gateway for external S3. Could also enable node-local egress for model hosts.

leo: implemented quick probe tweak on the sidecar that serves /ready (bumped initialDelaySeconds  from 10 -> 60 and failureThreshold  from 3 -> 8) and added a jittered backoff to the initContainer pulling models. Rolling patch started.

maya: after the patch ALB stopped deregistering targets for the next 20min window. CloudWatch NAT metrics showed a drop in concurrent active connections and conntrack entries stabilized. No further 503 spikes in that pool.

julia: follow-up items:
- runbook: if ALB 503 spike -> check conntrack, ip_local_port_range, NAT gateway EIP utilization, model-download concurrency, and readinessProbe timings.
- long-term: evaluate hosting model artifacts on EFS/FSx in-region or using a dedicated egress pool with extra NAT IPs for the GPU pool. Consider pre-warm DaemonSet or a shared sidecar to centralize downloads.

ops-jen: I'll add a short runbook and open infra task to add 2 spare EIPs + scale NAT gateway for the gpu-edge subnet in us-west-2. Also we'll add a small perf test to simulate concurrent model pulls and observe SNAT behavior.

maya: thanks — saved a lot of churn on the rollout. Filing notes in the incident and tagging the GPU rollout doc with mitigation steps.

leo: :thumbsup: good catch on correlating image/model pulls to SNAT pressure — that was the missing link.

julia: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see repeat.
